headline: 1,252 hospitalised in 24 hours as 4 more die from dengue
summary: The total death toll for the year has reached 111, with nearly 40,000 people hospitalised across Bangladesh since January.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), at least four more people died from dengue in the last 24 hours. During the same period, 1,252 patients were admitted to various hospitals across the country.

The distribution of new admissions includes 247 in Khulna, 227 in Dhaka outside city corporations, 194 in Chattogram, and 119 in Barishal. Dhaka North and South City Corporations recorded 101 and 135 admissions respectively.
Other regions reported 114 admissions in Rajshahi, 87 in Mymensingh, 27 in Rangpur, and six in Sylhet.
As of September 3, a total of 39,532 people have been hospitalised for dengue this year. The total number of deaths nationwide has reached 111.
While 36,387 patients have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, 1,034 people are currently receiving treatment in various facilities.

headline: Tk 6,000 fine: Minister's car fined for wrong-side driving in Dhaka
summary: Traffic police filed two cases against a Range Rover carrying Minister Rashiduzzaman Millat after it was found travelling against traffic on Circuit House Road.
details: Traffic police in Dhaka filed two cases against a Range Rover bearing registration Dhaka Metro-Gha-18-2125 after it was caught travelling on the wrong side of Circuit House Road.
The vehicle, which belonged to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism, was carrying Minister Rashiduzzaman Millat at the time it was stopped at around 9:08 am.
The driver, Arif Hossain, was fined a total of Tk 6,000, with Tk 3,000 imposed for each of the two separate offences, including reckless driving.

Traffic officials described the move as unprecedented, noting they could not recall any previous instance in Bangladesh where a minister's vehicle was formally charged for driving on the wrong side of the road.
While there have been reports of ministerial vehicles ignoring traffic rules to avoid congestion, these incidents typically did not result in legal cases.
Senior police officials stated that this action serves as a clear message that traffic laws apply equally to everyone, regardless of their status or position in government.
caption:
A minister's car was caught driving on the wrong side of the road in Dhaka—and this time, the police actually filed a case.

Traffic police in Dhaka filed two cases against a Range Rover bearing registration Dhaka Metro-Gha-18-2125 after it was caught travelling on the wrong side of Circuit House Road.

The vehicle, which belonged to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism, was carrying Minister Rashiduzzaman Millat at the time it was stopped at around 9:08 am.

The driver, Arif Hossain, was fined a total of Tk 6,000, with Tk 3,000 imposed for each of the two separate offences, including reckless driving.

Traffic officials described the move as unprecedented, noting they could not recall any previous instance in Bangladesh where a minister's vehicle was formally charged for driving on the wrong side of the road.

While there have been reports of ministerial vehicles ignoring traffic rules to avoid congestion, these incidents typically did not result in legal cases.

Senior police officials stated that this action serves as a clear message that traffic laws apply equally to everyone, regardless of their status or position in government.
